explanation: Under the UN's global labelling system it marks acute toxicity, while a flame marks flammable products. Radiation has its own sign, a three-bladed trefoil.

claims.text: A skull and crossbones on a label warns that the contents are poisonous.
The skull and crossbones does not warn of fire risk, radiation or electric shock.
In the UN's Globally Harmonized System of Classification and Labelling of Chemicals, the skull and crossbones pictogram marks acute toxicity.
In the Globally Harmonized System a flame pictogram marks flammable substances.
The radiation warning symbol is a three-bladed trefoil.
